audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff read HARD while breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t both said 'Even matchup - difficulty 5.5/10', against a 61.54% win rate over 26 games.
audit.why: 61.54% over a 26-game sample is Kassadin's best matchup in this slice, and the reason is structural: Galio's damage is magic, so Void Stone's reduction and Null Sphere's magic shield both apply at full value. HARD was flatly wrong.
audit.corrected: full.diff HARD -> EVEN, matching the rest of the file.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appeared anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Shield of Durand is 18/17/16/15/14s, Justice Punch and Winds of War are both 11/10/9/8/7s, and Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s. Justice Punch on 11 seconds against a 5-second Riftwalk is why you get two blinks per engage attempt.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, report[9].t and loading now carry them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three gaps. (1) content.early calls Null Sphere a 'spellshield' - it is a damage shield that absorbs magic, not a spell shield, and a player who believes it blocks a whole ability will walk into Justice Punch. (2) Nothing said Shield of Durand is a CHARGE that only taunts NEARBY enemies on release, so stepping outside the 275 radius while he holds it denies the taunt entirely. (3) Nothing said Justice Punch stops on the first enemy champion it meets, and that being knocked up means no Riftwalk until you land.
audit.why: Riot: 'Galio charges a defensive stance, moving slowly. Upon releasing the charge, Galio will taunt and damage nearby enemies'; 'Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters'; Null Sphere 'grants a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage'.
audit.corrected: Fixed the spellshield wording and wrote both mechanics into report[5].t, dosFull[0].d, loading and content.spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.spikes[2].text described his tankiness as 'Void Stone-irrelevant', which reads as though Kassadin's passive does nothing here. It is the opposite.
audit.why: Every damage source Galio has is magic - Colossal Smash, Winds of War, Shield of Durand and Hero's Entrance - so Void Stone's reduction and the Null Sphere shield both apply at full value. That is the whole reason this matchup wins 61%.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[2].t read 'Forget Mercs flip his CC math' with a description about juggernauts that had nothing to do with it.
audit.why: The actual mistake in this lane is poking into a charging Shield of Durand, which feeds the release and holds you in the taunt radius.

edits.before: Galio's Q, Winds of War, is the whole early game — its converging tornado pokes you off the wave, and although Null Sphere's spellshield can soak one gust, the orb costs far too much mana to keep answering at levels 1-3. You have no escape and no real sustain yet, so do not step up to trade autos into his empowered Colossal Smash. Last-hit at max range, time your Q shield to eat his poke, and accept you are losing these levels — this is a champion you survive, not contest.
edits.after: Galio's Q, Winds of War, is the whole early game - its converging tornado pokes you off the wave, and although Null Sphere's shield soaks the magic damage of one gust, it is a damage shield and not a spell shield, and the orb costs far too much mana to keep answering at levels 1-3. You have no escape and no sustain yet, so do not step up into his empowered Colossal Smash. Last-hit at max range, time the Q shield for his poke, and accept you are losing these levels.

edits.after: Riftwalk gives you an escape: Shield of Durand only taunts what is still inside 275 when he releases the charge, so blink out while he holds it rather than trading under his empowered Colossal Smash.

notes: 'Null Sphere's spellshield' in content.early was the most misleading line: Null Sphere grants a damage shield that absorbs magic, not a spell shield, and the two behave completely differently against Justice Punch. Also corrected 'Void Stone-irrelevant tankiness' - every damage source Galio owns is magic, so Void Stone and the Q shield are at their most valuable in this exact matchup, which is what a 61.54% win rate is measuring. Skipped the _missing-interactions line 'Galio can cancel your Null Sphere (Q) with Shield of Durand (W), Hero's Entrance (R)': it comes from a channel flag on Null Sphere that misfires - Riot's text says Null Sphere interrupts channels, it is not one. Whether Null Sphere can interrupt Galio's own Shield of Durand charge is not answerable from the kit data, so I did not write it - logged in unverified.
